trigger.eyebrow: A timely reason to improve the experience
trigger.title: Digital instructions are becoming part of the machinery conversation.
trigger.body: The EU Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027. It permits instructions in digital form under specified conditions and retains requirements around access, download, printing and paper instructions on request. Video can help explain a machine, but it does not replace the required instructions or create compliance by itself.

transcript: A machine is easier to understand when you can follow the work. Start with one part entering the line.
Inside, a sequence of stages turns a complicated system into a process you can see.
The important story is how the work moves from one stage to the next: what comes in, what happens in between, and what comes out.
When customers can follow that sequence, they have a clearer way to understand where the machine fits and what to ask next.
DHEE helps industrial teams make complex products easier to understand. Start with one machine and one clear story.

faqs.question: Does the Machinery Regulation require video instructions?
faqs.answer: No. The regulation allows instructions to be supplied in digital form under specified conditions, but it does not require video. Video can be an additional explanatory resource; it does not replace the required instructions.

faqs.question: Can digital instructions replace paper instructions?
faqs.answer: The regulation permits digital instructions if its conditions are met, including that users can access, download and print them. A manufacturer must provide paper instructions free of charge on request, within the regulation's stated period. Machinery intended for non-professional users also has additional paper-instruction requirements for the relevant safety information. Confirm the requirements for your product with your compliance team.

faqs.question: What should the sample video show?
faqs.answer: Use a real, approved machine reference and focus on one audience question: what the machine does, how a workflow fits together or what a new customer should understand first. Product and safety claims need review by your team.

faqs.question: Can the same story support sales and customer education?
faqs.answer: The core product story can be adapted for different moments. A sales overview, a setup orientation and a service explainer should each be shaped for their audience and purpose.

cta.title: Which machine should we make clearer first?
cta.body: Bring one product, one audience and one question your team hears often. We can use that to shape a focused first story.
